newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany, U.S. planning integrated air defence unit.
newsitem.headline: Germany, U.S. planning integrated air defence unit.

text.p: Germany and the United States are working on plans to create an integrated air defence unit that would be used for missions to crisis regions and the protection of NATO air space, a Defence Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
Confirming a report in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, the Defence Ministry said the unit would comprise a force of about 500 soldiers from three German and two U.S. air force squadrons.
The unit, to be called the "German-American Air Defence unit", will be equipped with Patriot, Hawk and Roland air defence missiles from the two countries.
Germany will bring its missiles along with nearly 300 soldiers into the unit while the U.S. will contribute two Patriot missile squadrons and an unspecified number of troops to the alliance.

The command would be shared by German and American officers and alternate between the two sides every three years. It has not yet been determined where the unit would be stationed or exactly how many soldiers will be included.

"There are several objectives being fulfilled," a Defence Ministry spokesman said. "It would further U.S.-German cooperation, strengthen European defence, and improve our inter-operability with the U.S. forces."

Germany and France formed a German-Franco brigade made up of about 4,500 soldiers in 1991. The U.S.-German air defence unit would be the first such integrated alliance with German and American forces, the spokesman said.

"A memorandum of understanding should be completed by the end of 1997 or the start of 1998 and the squadron will then be built up step by step," the spokesman said. "It is expected to be fully operational by the turn of the century."

The FAZ said that German defence ministry officials were eager to strengthen ties with the U.S. forces, which are still considered to be close despite a sharp decline in the number of American troops in Germany since the end of the Cold War.
There was also concern that the recent emphasis Germany has placed on building ties with French and other European armies had in recent years eclipsed to some extent German-U.S. military ties.
